description: Oracle attention driver chain, balanced variant. Run in-process by `contenox mission fire --oracle` on a mission's attention ask, with the ask event as input. The shape is chain-agent-run's proven agentic loop stripped to one tool: oracle_loop (chat, budget 3 tool rounds) → oracle_tools (execute) → back; a chat-text reply routes through oracle_correct, whose deterministic oracle.verdict_state gate either ends a settled contract or feeds a machine-register correction back for a bounded retry (budget 2); oracle_recovery gets 2 more rounds. Every invalid submit_verdict call comes back as {accepted:false, message} naming what to fix; a policy denial comes back as a plain denied-per-policy result (the loop then submits wait). No verdict within the budgets ends WAIT-equivalent: nothing executed, the ask stays with a human. Bounded by hitl-policy-oracle.json (deny-all except oracle.submit_verdict/verdict_state; no shell, no filesystem).

tasks.description: The review loop: judge the ask, submit exactly one verdict via oracle.submit_verdict. tool_call executes; chat text routes to the verdict_state gate (settled ends, open corrects and retries).
tasks.system_instruction:
You are a task processing engine talking to other machines.

INPUT: one attention ask as JSON. Fields: askId (the durable ask), missionId, agentName (the asking unit), intent (the mission's stated intent), summary (the question), detail (context; may be absent).

DECISION: the question is ROUTINE only when the mission's stated intent together with the ask's summary and detail states or directly implies the answer — no new judgment, nothing destructive, nothing outside the mission's scope.

OUTPUT: exactly one oracle.submit_verdict tool call; never chat text.
{"verdict":"wait","askId":"<askId from INPUT>"} — the question waits for a human.
{"verdict":"answer","answer":"<one short plain sentence the unit can act on>","askId":"<askId from INPUT>"} — the question is ROUTINE.
The answer is plain words on one line. When unsure: wait.
RESULT: the tool returns {accepted, outcome, message}. accepted true ends the task: reply DONE. accepted false means nothing was recorded: read message, correct the call, and submit again — except when message states the answer was denied per policy, where the next call is {"verdict":"wait","askId":"<askId from INPUT>"}.

tasks.description: Execute the submit_verdict call and append its result — an acknowledgment, or a corrective result naming exactly what was invalid — to the chat history.
Deterministic gate on a chat-text reply: oracle.verdict_state reports the bound contract. settled → end; open → the rendered machine-register correction loops back as oracle_loop's next input.
Recovery loop — the main loop's budget is spent or a step failed; two more rounds to land one valid verdict, then the chain ends WAIT-equivalent.
